info.name: Tasklist API
info.description:
REST API for a small task management application.

Five endpoints: list tasks, create a task, read one task, toggle completion, delete a task. Responses use HATEOAS links (RFC 8288 relations) and errors use RFC 7807 ProblemDetails.

## Setup

1. Start the API: `dotnet run --project src/TaskList.Api` (listens on http://localhost:5113).
2. The database is created and seeded automatically on first launch.
3. Run the requests top to bottom. The collection variables capture IDs automatically, so the Create -> Toggle -> Delete chain works without manual copying.

## Variables

- `baseUrl` — defaults to http://localhost:5113. Change once here if you run on a different port.
- `createdTaskId` — captured automatically from the Create response; consumed by Read one, Toggle, and Delete.
- `seededTaskId` — captured automatically from the first item of the List response, so the read-only requests work against seeded data without depending on the Create chain.

## Following HATEOAS links

Each item in a response carries a `links` array, and every link includes its HTTP `method`: `self` is GET, `toggle` is POST, `delete` is DELETE, `create` is POST. The `href` is an absolute URL, so it is ready to call as-is.

When you click a raw `href` from a response in Postman, Postman opens it as a GET regardless of the link's `method`. Calling a POST-only route (like toggle) with GET correctly returns 405 Method Not Allowed — that is the API behaving properly, not a bug; the route exists but does not accept GET. To follow a link, use the matching request in this collection (already set to the correct method), or set the method manually to the value named in that link's `method` field.

## Folder order

| Folder | Purpose |
|---|---|
| 1. Health | Liveness and readiness probes. Run first to confirm the API is up. |
| 2. Tasks — happy path | List, create, read, toggle, delete in the order a client would use them. |
| 3. Error cases | The validation (422), duplicate-title (409), and not-found (404) paths, each asserted. |

item.name: 1. Health
item.description: Orchestration probes. No auth. `/health/live` checks the process is up with no dependency checks; `/health/ready` also verifies SQLite is reachable. Run these first to confirm the API is listening before exercising the task endpoints.

request.description: Returns 200 with body `Healthy` if the process is alive. No database or dependency checks.
Returns 200 if SQLite is reachable, 503 otherwise. Use this for orchestration readiness gating.

item.name: 2. Tasks — happy path
item.description: The five task endpoints in the order a client would use them. Create captures the new id into `createdTaskId`; List captures the first seeded id into `seededTaskId`. Toggle and Delete then run against `createdTaskId` with no manual copying.

request.description:
Returns 200 with `{ data, links }`. `data` is the tasks ordered by creation time descending; each task carries its own HATEOAS `links` (self, toggle, delete). `links` at the envelope level holds collection-level relations (self, create). There is no `count` field; the client derives it from `data.length`.

Each link includes its `method` (self=GET, toggle=POST, delete=DELETE). Clicking a raw href in Postman opens it as GET, so a click on the toggle/delete link returns 405 — use this collection's Toggle and Delete requests (already set to the right method) to follow those relations. See the collection overview for details.

exec: pm.test('no count field (contract is { data, links })', () => pm.expect(body).to.not.have.property('count'));

request.description:
Creates a task. Returns 201 with a Location header and the created `TaskResponse` body: `{ id, title, isCompleted, createdAt, links }`. The new id is captured into `createdTaskId` for the Toggle and Delete requests below.

Note: if you run this twice without deleting, the second call returns 409 (duplicate title) — see folder 3.

exec: pm.test('body has id, title, isCompleted, createdAt, links', () => {
pm.test('new task starts not completed', () => pm.expect(body.isCompleted).to.be.false);

request.description: Returns 200 with a single `TaskResponse` for the task created above, or 404 if the id does not exist. Uses the `createdTaskId` captured by the Create request.
Flips `isCompleted` for the task. Returns 200 with the updated `TaskResponse`, or 404 if the id does not exist. Run it twice to see the value flip back.
Deletes the task. Returns 204 No Content on success, or 404 if the id does not exist. Deleting an already-deleted id returns 404.

item.name: 3. Error cases
item.description: The error paths, each asserted. Validation failures (422) come from FluentValidation as an HttpValidationProblemDetails with an `errors` map. Domain failures (409 duplicate title, 404 not found) come through the Result pipeline as RFC 7807 ProblemDetails where `title` is the error code (e.g. `task.duplicate_title`) and `detail` is the human-readable message.

request.description: An empty title fails validation. Returns 422 Unprocessable Entity with `application/problem+json`, an `errors` object keyed by field, and the message "Title is required."

A title longer than 200 characters fails validation. Returns 422 with the message "Title must be 200 characters or fewer." The 200-character limit is a single source of truth shared by the API validator and the database schema.

This title is one of the tasks created by the seeder, so against a freshly seeded database it returns 409 Conflict on the first run. No need to run it twice. The response is `application/problem+json` with `title` = `task.duplicate_title` and `detail` = "A task with the title 'Review pull requests from Q2 sprint backlog' already exists." The title comparison is case-insensitive and trimmed.

exec: pm.test('title is the duplicate-title error code', () => pm.expect(body.title).to.eql('task.duplicate_title'));
pm.test('detail names the conflicting title', () => pm.expect(body.detail).to.include('Review pull requests from Q2 sprint backlog'));

request.description: An id that does not exist returns 404 with `application/problem+json`, `title` = `task.not_found`, and a detail message naming the id.

exec: pm.test('title is the not-found error code', () => pm.expect(body.title).to.eql('task.not_found'));

request.description: Deleting an id that does not exist returns 404 with the same ProblemDetails shape as the read path.
